followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the query and the two models' capability/preference profiles.

The query is a general evaluative/advisory question (is ice cream good for a healthy diet) with an explicit demand for a direct, non-hedging answer. That maps to reasoning quality and instruction-following rather than to a specialized task family like extraction or moderation.

On the relevant benchmarks, Plover-235B is clearly stronger: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3 — relevant to "follow my no-hedging instruction"), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2). These are above the noise threshold.

I also checked the task-preference notes for anything that might offset that edge. Plover's only notable preference is a flat response to distasteful content, which is irrelevant here. Avocet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, and this question is fairly open-ended — a slight mark against routing it there. So both capability and preference pointed the same direction, and I went with Plover.
